cands.bio: Republican member of the Alabama House of Representatives for District 102 since November 2018. Former Satsuma police chief and Mobile County Sheriff's Office captain. Wikipedia lists him as police chief of Creola.

controversies.text: In May 2021, Mobile County Sheriff Sam Cochran removed Stringer as a captain. The sheriff's office cited "different political views held by his administration" and did not name them. Stringer said Cochran told him it was because he sponsored a bill ending gun-carry permits. He said he would keep pushing it.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Shane Stringer was raised or when he began living in Alabama as an adult. We found no dated work history, and the pages do not say when he served as Satsuma police chief or when he became Creola police chief. We found no statements from him on data centers, homestead taxes, land ownership, growth and development, immigration or H-1B, police funding, abortion, or school choice. His Ballotpedia page shows no 2026 survey responses and no endorsements. We found no documented actions on those issues beyond the constitutional carry bill reported by Wikipedia. The reason given for his 2021 firing rests on a single Wikipedia sentence with no corroborating news report.
